stories.title: U.S. to tell partners they must pick sides in AI race with China: Reuters
stories.simple_summary: The U.S. government is telling its allies they need to choose between supporting American AI companies or Chinese ones, rather than working with both.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to politicians and large companies — nothing you need to act on right now.

stories.title: Woman claims her stepfather used Grok to transform childhood photo into explicit imagery
stories.simple_summary: A woman says someone used an AI tool called Grok to turn her childhood photo into inappropriate imagery without her permission.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows a real danger of AI tools: people can misuse them to create harmful fake images, which is why you should be careful about what photos you share online.

stories.title: Have a laugh at AI’s expense by roleplaying as a chatbot
stories.simple_summary: There's a new game where you pretend to be an AI chatbot and see if a human can tell the difference.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect your daily life — it's just entertainment that pokes fun at AI.

stories.title: Anthropic shares more details about how Claude’s new watermarks will work
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic (a company that makes an AI called Claude) is adding invisible watermarks to its AI-created content so people can tell it's AI-made.
stories.why_it_matters: This could help you identify when something was created by AI rather than a real person, which is useful for avoiding misinformation.

stories.title: SpaceX officially closes its Cursor acquisition
stories.simple_summary: SpaceX bought a software company called Cursor that helps programmers write code using AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech workers — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Prediction: These 3 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks Will Rise More than 30% Before 2026 Is Over
stories.simple_summary: Someone is predicting that three AI-related stocks will go up in value by more than 30% before 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: This is investment advice, not news — only relevant if you're buying stocks.

stories.title: Secondhand booksellers in UK and Ireland suspect AI firms behind ‘strange’ bulk orders
stories.simple_summary: Used bookstores in the UK and Ireland noticed AI companies are buying lots of old books in bulk, possibly to use them for training AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI companies are collecting large amounts of text from books to teach their systems — it may affect authors and publishers, but probably won't change your life directly.

stories.title: AI vs the people
stories.simple_summary: The headline doesn't give enough detail to explain what this is about.
stories.why_it_matters: Can't tell from the headline alone whether this matters to you.

stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg has an Instagzam
stories.simple_summary: Instagram changed its logo and the new version looks quite different from the old, famous one.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't involve AI — it's just Instagram redesigning their logo, which doesn't affect how you use the app.

stories.title: You can now turn off Google Gemini’s visible watermarks
stories.simple_summary: Google is now letting you hide the watermark (a small sparkly mark) that appears on images, videos, and music created by its AI tools.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Google's AI to make images or videos, you can now remove the obvious AI-made label if you want to.

stories.title: Google will now allow users to remove visible watermark from its AI generations
stories.simple_summary: Google is letting people turn off the visible watermark on AI-created content, but invisible tracking marks will still stay.
stories.why_it_matters: Similar to item 9 — affects people who create AI images, but doesn't impact most everyday users.

stories.title: Does Mark Zuckerberg really believe AI is ‘for everyone’?
stories.simple_summary: Meta released a free AI model anyone can download and use, and Mark Zuckerberg says AI should be available to everyone, not just big companies.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have a computer and want to experiment with AI, this means free tools are becoming available, though most people won't need this.
